lessons.boundary: The closure holds on the declared localization. Residual D!=0, main A*B!=0 and omitted pivot/projective faces remain unresolved. Filenames ending modular3 can contain cutoff-four data; read max_order and field labels.
lessons.reopen_when: A new target concerns an unresolved residual chart or requires the ambient cutoff-four scheme itself.

lessons.title: Compute all source-degree cutoffs with one incremental echelon
lessons.when: The same tangent space is tested at many degree cutoffs for its unique source trivializer.
lessons.use: Construct the tangent basis and coefficient rows of adj(DF)G once, group the rows by source degree, then insert them in descending degree order. Rank above each cutoff gives the whole filtered profile without solving a new tangent system. Reuse the retained p=32003 profiles and CSK1 exact rational seed degrees.
lessons.avoid: Reconstructing the tangent matrix for each cutoff or redoing the rational seed gauges as if they were only modular observations.
lessons.boundary: The full cutoffs 33/48/63 remain single-prime results. Source-only first-order degree is not the optimal two-sided filtration, and finite exhaustion does not erase stable moduli or prove algebraization.
lessons.reopen_when: A characteristic-zero full-profile certificate, a new coefficient box or a precisely defined two-sided filtration is in scope.

lessons.title: Keep lower-order kernel choices in higher deformation obstructions
lessons.when: A greedy formal lift fails, or quadratic and cubic homogeneous layers are passed to a component calculation.
lessons.use: Retain the lower-order free kernel parameters when formulating the next obstruction. Use the known seed family as a positive control. The quartic generic compiler already records 22 normal quadrics and 305 cubic equations; its 327-generator homogeneous-layer input is retained, together with the failed primary-decomposition attempt.
lessons.avoid: Calling a fourth-order failure of one chosen correction a universal obstruction, identifying the layer ideal with the completed local ideal, or interpreting transverse tangent excess as proof of embedded nilpotents.
lessons.boundary: A reduced family need not be a component; excess tangent dimension can come from thickness, other branches or both. The 12 GB failed standard-basis run produced no radical or primary decomposition.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact calculation retains all lower-order choices and proves the claimed completed-scheme or algebraization implication.

lessons.title: Read terminal stopping reasons before treating unused adaptive capacity as work
lessons.when: A historical runbook calls a campaign active or quotes its maximum possible box count.
lessons.use: Use the existing terminal reporter on retained checkpoints. The record-scale cohort completed all48 curves at2352 certified boxes with zero gains; every initial no-gain wave stopped its curve. The32/8/8 score strata are fully reported. Bind roster, wave proofs, stopping reasons and completed exposure before interpreting a comparison.
lessons.avoid: Restarting a completed cohort to fill its11760-box adaptive maximum, treating a RUNNING snapshot as live state, or rebuilding the million-parameter intake to learn a retained outcome.
lessons.boundary: A completed no-gain detector result is a bounded miss. It establishes neither an upper rank bound nor score equivalence. Reporter hash checks reuse prior certificates; they are not a fresh independent arithmetic replay.
lessons.reopen_when: A different detector or population has a separately declared hypothesis, finite budget and proof plan.

lessons.title: Preserve frozen assignments while separating changed coordinate measurements
lessons.when: A historical protocol source hash differs after an explicit backend amendment.
lessons.use: Audit population, assignment, context and budgets unchanged; permit only declared source replacements whose historical bytes match the pinned revision. Keep raw and amended-runtime checkpoints separate. The rescue audit verifies the2239 assignments and historical66 clean zeros without Sage, while reporting current readiness as NOT_CERTIFIED. Preserve the exact301-class rescue set and its separate specialized reranking. The CRT half-lattice worker likewise writes a separate pointed-runtime ledger; its frozen v3 analyzer still requires the original v3 ledger.
lessons.avoid: Overwriting a frozen protocol to make its old builder --check pass, merging raw boxes into changed coordinate boxes, treating12 assigned historical zeros as12 compatible current inputs, or reconstructing absent base chunks during cleanup.
lessons.boundary: No rescue chart has run. The current worker recomputes the complete generic parity census rather than loading a persisted table. Assignment without outcome inputs does not erase that the protocol was frozen after the base checkpoint was known.
lessons.reopen_when: Compatible base evidence has been recovered and identity-checked, or a separately scoped implementation reuses a certified order keyed by exact generic Gram, basis and labels.

lessons.title: Normalize each local divisor before discarding a prime
lessons.when: An RR fake-Kummer panel rejects a place because one evaluation is nonunit or its basepoint has negative valuation.
lessons.use: Normalize the sextic and each divisor separately by rational prime powers. Omit only nonunit divisors; for negative basepoint valuation use the scalar-equivalent anchor1-T/T0. This recovered152 previously skipped pairs without new primes or points. At certified good reduction, compare the attained rank with the complete local dimension and independently check the fake kernel.
lessons.avoid: Requiring every inherited generator to be a unit, discarding a whole prime unnecessarily, or calling failure of this model reduction test intrinsic bad reduction.
lessons.boundary: The frozen panel closes553/640 pairs. The83 failed reduction tests and four anchor cases remain unresolved. Rational-scalar normalization is justified in the stated fake squareclass quotient; its true-image conclusion also uses the proved kernel statement.
lessons.reopen_when: An unresolved anchor or reduction case has a certified alternative local model, with the same class maps and completeness checks.

lessons.title: Reuse complete local images without collapsing the remaining global problem
lessons.when: A proposed RR incidence detector asks for classes outside the inherited image at an already certified place.
lessons.use: Reuse the553 complete good-prime images and all ten real and2-adic images: the inherited subgroup spans each. Preserve true/fake kernel data. A global comparison still needs simultaneous compatibility in a complete supported squareclass space, including unramified class contributions; the inherited combination can differ from place to place.
lessons.avoid: Searching for an outside-inherited class at a place already proved fully spanned, identifying local proxies with the original global fields, or replacing global completeness with trial-prime support or known rational classes.
lessons.boundary: The known rational Kummer dimension is18. A certified full Selmer dimension18 would give exact Jacobian rank18 and zero Sha[2]; a larger dimension is not automatically Sha. Prepared equation replay does not prove any local image or global Selmer group.
lessons.reopen_when: A complete global algorithm or a new unresolved-place certificate supplies an obligation beyond the already closed local panels.

lessons.title: Test proposal recall and actual integral subgroup identity before tuning scores
lessons.when: A low-height or common-cover lattice candidate is proposed as a recovered generic family.
lessons.use: Check the full proposal ledger against the frozen masked control. The two generators peak at rank12 intersections8 and10; the second comparison covers all1928 rank12 proposals, so rescoring cannot recover an absent space. Keep the successful older graph-consensus primitive closure and its index2048 actual subgroup separate. Use Curve302's completed alternative MW17 parent for construction recovery.
lessons.avoid: Promoting a containing higher-rank space to exact recovery, recognizing Fermigier from index2^11 alone, or rerunning failed proposal generators to rediscover Curve302's already proved parent.
lessons.boundary: Any independent rank-r set in one nonzero parity class forces index divisible by2^(r-1) in its primitive closure. A projected Schur quotient is not an exact integral orthogonal complement. Neither rounded heights nor bounded proposal failure proves nonexistence.
lessons.reopen_when: A new generator passes a declared control at the exact requested rank and actual integral subgroup, with a separate geometric reconstruction proof.

lessons.title: Batch coset norms and sieve exact membership while preserving relation content
lessons.when: A fixed lattice proposal searches many shifted representatives or tests a large pool against candidate spaces.
lessons.use: Precompute shifts and their norms, then evaluate each coset with q(c+s)=q(s)+2s^T Hc+q(c) and stable ordering. Reuse an exact integer kernel: mod1009 matrix products reject nonmembers before exact integer products on survivors. Keep unit relations v_i plus or minus v_j equals v_k literal; dividing content would turn a+b=2c into a false unit edge.
lessons.avoid: Repeating full norm/rank calculations for every representative, treating the support-at-most-two shifted box as complete CVP, or using bounded qfminim's second field as the minimum.
lessons.boundary: The search explicitly minimizes returned norms. Agreement of80- and100-digit height balls is numerical evidence, not an interval-certified cutoff. verify_low_height_mw_sublattices --check rebuilds balls, minima and finite reductions; it is not a cheap metadata check.
lessons.reopen_when: The exact basis or proposal domain changes, or a new completeness claim requires certified numerical bounds and an appropriately scoped replay.

lessons.title: Keep section labels and ordinate branches fixed before stacking fibres
lessons.when: Finite reductions from several parameter values are stacked to prove generic independence.
lessons.use: Use one source-root permutation and exact rational-function ordinate branches. The Mestre adapter preserves both. The corrected13 probes have rank11; the old sorted-root and positive-square-root probes still have matrix rank13 but do not specialize one common coefficient relation.
lessons.avoid: Sorting section columns independently at each fibre, choosing square-root signs numerically, or treating tests that reproduce the old matrix as a valid generic proof.
lessons.boundary: A fixed coherent matrix of full column rank plus torsion exclusion proves the stated lower bound. Rank defects alone give neither dependence nor an upper bound. The rejected entry point now fails rather than emitting a false conclusion.
lessons.reopen_when: A fixed labelled section list has a new exact certificate for the stronger claimed rank.

lessons.title: Prove recursive section identities using explicit degree bounds
lessons.when: Expanded Mestre two-section residuals would create tens or hundreds of thousands of terms.
lessons.use: Keep the monic-square and triangular ordinate recursions. Bound the numerator degree after the declared denominator clearing, then check more distinct admissible exact values than that degree. The Fermigier component uses1141 values for bound1140; the diameter235 component uses1099 for bound1080. Retain excluded poles and the leading-square condition.
lessons.avoid: Treating a Hensel or Pade fit alone as a global identity, expanding residuals unnecessarily, or dropping D=w^2 after projecting to abscissa equations.
lessons.boundary: An identity proves an incidence component, not independence of its sections. Jacobian rank and finite jets do not settle the full component without the later exact argument.
lessons.reopen_when: A changed parameterization comes with a new denominator and degree proof.

lessons.title: Separate parameter aliases and nonminimal factors from source discrepancies
lessons.when: A Fermigier specialization or raw quartic discriminant appears to give a different family or bad-fibre pattern.
lessons.use: Reuse the exact adapter u=s/2 and retained coefficients. For Y^2=X^3-27IX-27J the raw discriminant scale is(607392u)^12, since c4_raw=1296I. The twelfth-power scalar and u factor are coordinate artifacts. The exact generic arithmetic rank12 is already proved separately.
lessons.avoid: Reusing the stale202464 scale, counting literal s and adapter u as unrelated candidates, or treating completed rank computations as a resolution of the paper convention.
lessons.boundary: Literal printed shift19754/39 and reconstruction shift39508/39 give different j-invariants; the source factor-two discrepancy remains unresolved. Benchmark GP conductor calls are not metadata checks.
lessons.reopen_when: Primary-source provenance explains the convention, or an explicit new coordinate map is proved.

lessons.title: Recover an unlabeled subgroup through exact relation components
lessons.when: Comparing high-rank specializations when the intended generic subgroup, section labels and source surface are not supplied.
lessons.use: Enumerate a declared short-vector cloud, extract additive-relation components, and prune with finite quotient ranks and height-angle compatibility. Take exact primitive rational closures after each merge, then select by held-out relation replay per added rank. Verify the final subgroup by exact integer linear algebra and elliptic-curve arithmetic.
lessons.avoid: Inferring a generic rank from a short-vector shell, treating numerical heights or selector outputs as a theorem, retuning after inspecting a failed target, or identifying a source surface before the subgroup survives exact replay.
lessons.boundary: The frozen controls recover a rank-12 Fermigier primitive closure and a rank-16 R17 component before exact completion. Two frozen target sets failed their own recurrence gates; this does not exclude another common primitive subgroup or recover a new family.
lessons.reopen_when: A new, independently frozen target set has declared inputs, exact subgroup endpoints and a pass condition before target outcomes are inspected.

lessons.title: Treat a frozen score replay as calibration, not prospective screening
lessons.when: Assessing a parameter score using known high-rank controls while the remaining population has no exact endpoint labels.
lessons.use: Freeze the score, primitive parameter domain, tie policy and evaluation budgets before ranking. Record each known control's exact position and keep all unassayed parameters explicitly censored. Use a miss to retire that score for the stated family and protocol.
lessons.avoid: Calling a known control a prospective holdout, assigning rank zero to unassayed parameters, reporting classifier accuracy from censored data, or launching another broad score campaign after a bounded calibration miss.
lessons.boundary: The Fermigier replay ranks 60,815,684 primitive parameters and finds both known controls beyond 2.7 million in every recorded ordering. It rules out those frozen local scores for this stated calibration only; it is neither a rank bound nor a general prediction result.
lessons.reopen_when: A new score has a separately scoped prospective protocol, genuinely withheld families, exact endpoints and a declared decision rule.

lessons.title: Keep a mechanism-label holdout separate from the rank target
lessons.when: Using finite-cover visibility or another bounded mechanism label to prioritize a total-rank search.
lessons.use: Freeze the population, arithmetic duplicate groups, score and review budget before labels or control outcomes are opened. Evaluate the mechanism label on its own outcome-free holdout, then separately record the once-opened rank-control result. Retire the score for the total-rank objective if it succeeds only on the mechanism response.
lessons.avoid: Calling bisection-gain AUC or enrichment a total-rank predictor; treating a publicly known quarantined control as a human-blind discovery; retuning after opening that control; or assigning censored bounded misses a negative rank label.
lessons.boundary: The frozen R17 ranker generalized to its 5,000-row bisection-label holdout but missed the rank-28 control at a one-percent budget. It establishes that the measured bisection response differs from extreme total rank in this protocol, not that bisections, learned scores, or other families cannot help a rank search.
lessons.reopen_when: A separately committed target has outcome-free arithmetic grouping, genuinely unopen controls and a response that matches the proposed decision endpoint.

lessons.title: Check the target coset before lifting a missing section
lessons.when: An explicit section shell has the right rank but may have nontrivial index in its saturation.
lessons.use: Compute the exact shell lattice and target coset in the equation marking. The A11 identity shell has index five; enumerate the marked target coset to obtain the P.O=5 bridge and reuse the short group word.
lessons.avoid: Lifting an arbitrary missing-rank section or the earlier P.O=4 vector: neither necessarily generates the desired target with the retained shell.
lessons.boundary: The pole bound and coset exclusion concern this marked lattice. The orbit12 equation was subsequently constructed; the old elimination timeout is not a remaining gate.
lessons.reopen_when: A different marked subgroup or target changes the exact coset problem.

lessons.title: Reconstruct shared coefficient scales projectively
lessons.when: Exact modular section coefficients have monic denominators but coefficientwise rational reconstruction stalls.
lessons.use: Use simultaneous projective LLL on numerator and denominator coefficients, reject scales sharing a factor with the CRT modulus, then verify the rational section identity and reduction to every input prime. The q8 horizontal was recovered this way from22 primes without lifting its larger Abel trace.
lessons.avoid: Increasing all p-adic precision solely because a hidden common scale defeats independent coefficient reconstruction.
lessons.boundary: LLL proposes candidates; exact substitution and all-prime consistency certify the section. This is not a general uniqueness theorem or the subsequent RR/child construction.
lessons.reopen_when: New exact residues or a new projective normalization change the reconstruction problem.

lessons.title: Compile the chord pencil with a modular inverse
lessons.when: An exact horizontal is written x=X/Z^2, y=Y/Z^3 and the divisor ambient is known.
lessons.use: Impose AA*X=BB*Y modulo Z^2. When X is invertible modulo Z^2, solve AA=BB*Y/X modulo Z^2 directly and then impose the remaining degree and resolved vertical conditions. Verify the resulting h0=2 basis and quartic identity.
lessons.avoid: Starting a large elimination or Groebner calculation before exploiting the smooth collision congruence.
lessons.boundary: Invertibility, the complete line-bundle ambient and every vertical condition must be checked. The q8 example needs two independent resolved rows; the rootless q12 example has no vertical residual.
lessons.reopen_when: The marked divisor or its denominator/vertical support changes.

lessons.title: Certify the endpoint with the necessary construction data
lessons.when: A neighbour chain already reaches a rootless elliptic K3 equation.
lessons.use: Retain enough exact parent-to-child pointing and class transport to identify the source; recover and certify a rank17 basis directly at the endpoint. Reuse the completed source-identity, Picard-bound and saturation proofs before extending intermediate classifications.
lessons.avoid: Blocking a completed construction on an optional intermediate full MW basis, every neighbour orbit, or recovery of the entire polynomial shell.
lessons.boundary: The endpoint still needs exact equation, section identities, height Gram, source identity, Picard bound, torsion and saturation. Numerical lattice fingerprints alone do not replace those proofs.
lessons.reopen_when: The next edge or final source proof genuinely requires an omitted exact marking.

lessons.title: Compare invariant local images before refining CRT conditions
lessons.when: Comparing Kummer fingerprints across rational specializations.
lessons.use: Use the known-image source kernel at odd primes instead of raw uniformizer coordinates, which can change by a nonsquare. Use a p-maximal order at the place under audit, then freeze local-only discovery and disjoint confirmation draws before point outcomes.
lessons.avoid: Assuming t modulo p^3 fixes the desired local fingerprint, or paying for a global class/unit computation to audit one local prime.
lessons.boundary: Finite draws establish empirical stability only. The known-MW17 image is not the complete local Selmer condition.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact uniform local argument or a separately frozen parameter/prime protocol changes the gate.

lessons.title: Test detector sensitivity before interpreting a zero-event campaign
lessons.when: A bounded prospective point search returns no events.
lessons.use: Preserve the frozen cohort and protocol; apply the unchanged detector to committed positive controls and record what it actually sees. Freeze a stronger successor separately and keep binary detection, jump magnitude, upper-tail behavior and censoring gates distinct.
lessons.avoid: Treating2560 bounded misses as a rank theorem when the same call misses both known+12 controls, fitting a predictor to a constant response, or treating binary jump detection as evidence of rank32 sensitivity.
lessons.boundary: The first CRT experiment proves only its bounded zero-event outcome. The sealed MW17-only Selmer experiment has a separate unexecuted calibration gate.
lessons.reopen_when: A new detector passes predeclared controls and its compatible outcomes and inference rules are frozen.

lessons.title: Remove even uniformizer powers before evaluating cover fibres
lessons.when: Computing normalized fibres or quadratic character sums for z^2=b on a curve.
lessons.use: At an even-order zero or pole divide by its square uniformizer and evaluate the leading unit. Keep literal-square controls. On the determinant1236 candidate this repairs the false empty V4 screen and the rational fibre at4G.
lessons.avoid: Assigning character0 to every zero of b, or promoting finite Prym traces and an isomorphic cubic field to the required Shimura branch-point identity.
lessons.boundary: The candidate has exact divisor and fibre data; its particular modular CM branch-orbit identification remains open.
lessons.reopen_when: An exact characteristic-zero modular map or CM-value identity supplies the missing identification.

lessons.title: Prove omitted equations before promoting a finite lift
lessons.when: An overdetermined marked Weierstrass system has a unit maximal Jacobian minor.
lessons.use: Use the exact node/discriminant identity and prescribed jet orders to show all omitted residuals follow on the unit chart; then apply the formal implicit-function theorem. Preserve the source-shard identity and required mutual section intersections.
lessons.avoid: Treating tangent dimension one or a lift to7^8 as an infinite compatible branch, treating the branch as a QQ point, or identifying a displayed subgroup with its primitive closure.
lessons.boundary: NS0031 has a formal local branch but a full rational rank-19 marking is excluded by the separate corrected full stable quotient proof. Determinant500/720 rational reconstructions saturate to the wrong determinant20 lattice.
lessons.reopen_when: A different candidate or field passes its exact global rational-marking gate. Extending the completed NS0031 local box cannot reopen the excluded full rational rank-19 source over Q.

lessons.title: Retain specialization rank and saturation defects in the residual quotient
lessons.when: Comparing a generic subgroup, a certified specialized point group and residual Selmer dimensions.
lessons.use: First certify that the specialized generic subgroup M retains rank r. Record the free quotient rank separately from A/(M+2A), whose dimension is rank(A)-r+epsilon_M, with epsilon_M=dim A[2]+r-dim delta(M). Use a certified subgroup for lower bounds and a complete Selmer ambient space for upper bounds.
lessons.avoid: Calling an uncertified quotient gain a generic rank jump, or equating mod2 dimensions with new free directions before accounting for specialized saturation and torsion.
lessons.boundary: Generic saturation does not imply specialized saturation. Local-signature spans, incomplete descents and point-search misses do not supply a Selmer upper bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The generic subgroup, specialization, torsion certificate or complete Selmer ambient space changes.

lessons.title: Clear every known pivot before ranking residual signatures
lessons.when: Reducing finite local or fingerprint signatures modulo a known Mordell--Weil image.
lessons.use: Build an echelon basis for the known image and clear every present pivot in descending order before comparing or ranking residual signatures. Cross-check the result against rank(known plus candidates) minus rank(known) on small exhaustive fixtures.
lessons.avoid: Stopping at the first free coordinate and treating that partial remainder as a quotient representative or an independent residual direction. Early exit is valid only for a yes-or-no membership test.
lessons.boundary: This computes a quotient in the selected finite signature target. A zero residual only means that target does not distinguish the candidate from the known span; it proves neither a global square, a Selmer conclusion, nor a rank bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The target coordinates, known image, signature encoding, or quotient purpose changes.

lessons.title: Keep a pointed chart distinct from its actual two-covering map
lessons.when: Turning pointed quartics, translations or half-lattice search output into residual descent classes.
lessons.use: Record the birational point map phi and the actual covering map 2phi-P separately. Generic translations and the involution R->Q-R for Q in the generic subgroup preserve the residual label modulo the generic Kummer image. Deduplicate labels there, while retaining new independent point directions even when they share a label.
lessons.avoid: Treating a birational chart as the descent covering or counting every translated chart or new point as a new residual parity class.
lessons.boundary: A fixed actual two-covering maps into one coset of 2E(K). Its points can increase free rank without increasing the parity span. A coefficient-complexity claim must include the cost of the model and transport, since these can encode a known point.
lessons.reopen_when: The generic subgroup or covering cocycle changes, or a new independence certificate establishes a further free direction.

lessons.title: Use the full Cassels–Tate ambient space before claiming a rank upper bound
lessons.when: Interpreting a residual pairing matrix or selecting soluble and insoluble descent controls.
lessons.use: Certify actual Selmer membership and the Cassels–Tate construction, then distinguish the complete matrix from a restriction. A complete residual matrix of dimension s and rank 2a gives rank(E)<=r+s-2a-epsilon_M. A restricted matrix only constrains known points inside that subspace.
lessons.avoid: Using arbitrary Hilbert-symbol tensors as Cassels–Tate, treating a zero pairing or an isotropic subspace as a solubility certificate, or using a locally insoluble ambient squareclass as an insoluble Selmer control.
lessons.boundary: The residual radical modulo the full point space is 2Sha[4]; finiteness of Sha alone does not remove it. Known point classes pair to zero with all Selmer classes, so a point-only panel says nothing about the unknown complementary matrix.
lessons.reopen_when: An actual complete residual Selmer space, certified pairing entries or a new global covering witness is available.

lessons.title: Prove a nominal coordinate box contains candidates before spending search time
lessons.when: Using a height-bounded point routine after an exact projective transformation of a genus-one cover.
lessons.use: Translate the coordinate-height cap through the recorded transformations, fix a primitive parametrization, then use exact real-root and denominator bounds to determine whether the declared box contains any rational candidates. Retain that finite preflight separately from the routine's return value.
lessons.avoid: Calling a no-point return meaningful coverage when the transformed box is already empty, or treating global minimality of a genus-one model as a useful coordinate normalization for a bounded search.
lessons.boundary: The fixed-cubic audit proves emptiness only for six displayed projective-height boxes at 10^7. It does not decide any cover globally, construct a Sha obstruction, or make coordinate-height preflights interchangeable across other models and transformations.
lessons.reopen_when: The cover, coordinate transformation, height convention, or rational parametrization changes.

lessons.title: Use the complete smooth-atlas obstruction before enlarging a bisection search
lessons.when: Seeking a universal rank-jump mechanism by enumerating smooth rational bisections and their generic translates on the determinant1092 parent.
lessons.use: Reuse the completed 40917-orbit quotient and its finite union of degree-two parameter images. Generic translations preserve those images. The written thin-set argument already proves that non-thin rank-at-least18 fibres remain outside the entire smooth rational atlas.
lessons.avoid: Repeating or enlarging that completed smooth rational enumeration in order to explain every rank jump, or mistaking arbitrarily many translations for new parameter coverage.
lessons.boundary: The obstruction does not locate Curve302 in the atlas, give an effective height bound or exclude singular rational curves and positive-genus covers. It also does not restrict all pointed-quartic searches to smooth rational bisections.
lessons.reopen_when: The proposed construction leaves the certified smooth rational bisection class or asks a new explicitly scoped incidence question.

lessons.title: Preserve the exact fields needed for a small independent replay
lessons.when: A finite arithmetic witness reads large historical catalogues or optional local caches.
lessons.use: Extract the actual fields read by the checker, retaining unique row selectors and hashes of the original inputs and primary certificate. Provide a read-only verifier with a separate optional provenance audit. NS0031 uses eleven fields in 2771 bytes plus its 5575-byte certificate for the Clifford, 304-coset and prime19 computations.
lessons.avoid: Regenerating a missing catalogue to replay a small witness, accepting a projection with an ambiguous selector, or importing the original producer as the supposed independent implementation.
lessons.boundary: The projection preserves the selected data, not an independent proof of the source catalogue. The finite NS0031 replay does not prove the arithmetic K3 period map, global X0(37) rational-point classification, minimality or the rational37-isogenies. Optimized Python must fail before assertions can be skipped. The separate period-group review has now refuted the old containment; a finite arithmetic PASS cannot restore the K3 exclusion. The September14 exclusion instead uses a new full-stable group/model certificate and a separately retained unconditional Magma proof; the original finite PASS is not that proof.
lessons.reopen_when: The finite claim, required fields or source identities change. A new arithmetic theorem needs its own proof and replay; repeating the old finite check cannot repair the invalid norm-one containment.

lessons.title: Audit rank-screen identities and censoring before replaying calculations
lessons.when: Reusing a bounded rank screen or interpreting a command named --check.
lessons.use: Read the checker body and validate the complete roster, per-case input and execution identities, interval types, summary and ranking from the stored rows. Keep completed intervals, singleton exact ranks and censored cases as different counts. The V4 screen has62 completed intervals,17 exact ranks and2 named timeouts.
lessons.avoid: Trusting a saved total after checking only input hashes, counting timeout as rank zero, or rerunning the entire screen to inspect two unresolved cases.
lessons.boundary: A record audit does not independently prove PARI rank bounds. The original10-second limit includes Sage startup. Base-Jacobian rank and product-twist rank are separate questions; the later rank-zero product target55 does not settle timeout cases3 or30.
lessons.reopen_when: A new scoped calculation supplies a rank certificate for a specific unresolved curve or the stored universe/input identities change.

lessons.title: Reuse regulator squareclass obstructions before a full descent
lessons.when: A product twist has certified good reductions of analytic rank one and a height-preserving specialization argument.
lessons.use: Use stored complete L-polynomials first. Compare only reductions of analytic rank one: a hypothetical nontorsion section forces rank equality, and refined BSD gives its height the squareclass of p^(chi-1)*L_star/product(c_v). Incompatible squareclasses exclude every rational height. A rank-two reduction supplies no individual height squareclass; skip it before requesting another prime. The four-target sweep needed only one additional Frobenius polynomial. Reuse the completed17-product closure and empty section queue. Count each closed-place Tamagawa factor once.
lessons.avoid: Launching the old height-eight/height-ten solver or complete Selmer calculation after arithmetic rank zero is proved, or using an analytic-rank-two row in a rank-one height comparison.
lessons.boundary: Count each closed-place Tamagawa factor once. The argument needs complete certified L-polynomials, good reduction, height preservation and the stated finite-function-field theorem. Arithmetic rank zero does not imply geometric rank zero or Sha[2]=0.
lessons.reopen_when: A different target survives the exact eligible-prime comparison or the specialization hypotheses differ.

lessons.title: Use the full integral involution module for the Tate quotient
lessons.when: Computing a product-character obstruction from invariant and anti-invariant sections.
lessons.use: For a saturated basis B of ker_Z(1+S), solve 1-S=B*D integrally and compute coker(D); Smith factors are1 or2. The quotient can be represented by F2 functionals on the anti-invariant coordinates. If a stronger theorem already gives A-=0, conclude the quotient is zero directly.
lessons.avoid: Substituting a visible eigensublattice for the full MW group, equating a Selmer candidate space with the point-Kummer image, or taking exclusion of the zero class as existence of a nonzero class.
lessons.boundary: The supplied lattice must be full; checking S^2=1 and its Gram isometry cannot prove arithmetic fullness. All17 old products are arithmetically closed, although full Selmer groups were not computed.
lessons.reopen_when: A new target has a certified full involution lattice or complete actual point-Kummer image.

lessons.title: Replay stored integer relations and finite primes before rediscovery
lessons.when: An exact displayed-subgroup quotient certificate already contains the generic/split integer matrices and finite-reduction signatures.
lessons.use: Bind the original equation, ordered public point prefix, chart, split labels and integer matrix dimensions; verify each group-law relation, the original prime signatures, the torsion exclusion and the Smith quotient. Keep transport-only replay separate from exhaustive cover visibility and checkpoint each completed fibre.
lessons.avoid: Repeating a high-precision height solve or greedy prime search merely to recover an existing witness, silently accepting truncated/coerced integer rows, or rewriting generation hashes after a runtime chooses different valid primes.
lessons.boundary: Numerical heights propose relations; exact addition certifies them. A transport-only PASS says nothing new about complete cover visibility or full MW rank. The current runtime may select different primes from the original native audit, whose retained witnesses still replay. Original producer bytes remain pinned by three dependent certificates.
lessons.reopen_when: A new equation, ordered point set, generic basis or cover inventory changes the witness binding, or the exact retained relation fails.

lessons.title: Account for the discarded even discriminant part and retain polynomial witnesses
lessons.when: Excluding rational singular members of a genus-one bisection pencil through its discriminant squareclass.
lessons.use: Use the exact minimum-representative count m to identify m distinct split members, including q_infinity=h^2. Prove the finite discriminant has degree 22 and its even part has degree 2(m-1), so the known split members exhaust that part. Then exclude rational projective roots of the odd part by exact factorization/irreducibility or a good-prime root obstruction retaining the full and odd degrees. For an independent replay, retain the polynomial coefficients, decomposition identities and trace/model attachment, not only degrees or PASS fields. When a full homogeneous branch discriminant has no projective root at a single integral prime, exclude that entire pencil directly: no splitting off of the even part, comparison of distinct reduced parameters, or simultaneous good reduction across pencils is needed.
lessons.avoid: Dropping the even-multiplicity locus without explaining every split member, losing the point at infinity, or treating successful merging of 127,842 outcome records as an independent polynomial proof. The existing producers enumerate the whole norm-eight lattice before applying a prefix limit.
lessons.boundary: The recorded exclusion covers rational normalization through arithmetic genus one on alternate11952 and hidden103b2. It does not cover elliptic normalization or global genus-two injectivity. All 141 singular shards and both mergers passed integrity checks, but none of their trace records retains discriminant coefficients. The full49 moving norm12 pencils on alternate Q80 now have such individual witnesses:25 at521 and24 at523. Their73 retained discriminant polynomials and trace attachment are independently replayed; this extension leaves the old norm8 witness gap unchanged.
lessons.reopen_when: A new geometric row or a fixed exact polynomial witness supplies information beyond the completed exclusion; reconstructing all missing pencil data requires a separately scoped compute plan.

lessons.title: Compare full branch pencils, including moving zero contact, with projective and height certificates
lessons.when: Searching for two new directions on one quadratic cover from genus-one bisection pencils of height-eight or height-twelve trace parity.
lessons.use: Represent each binary-quartic branch family by its5-by5 coefficient matrix. At a good surface prime, normalize rational-function numerators and denominators jointly, verify preserved trace height and regular chord identities, and require nonzero images at every P1(Fp) point. Compare complete image buckets and intersect pair constraints with bitsets, retaining pairs incident to untested vertices. One invertible reduction per pencil proves within-pencil injectivity. A trace of height8 is identified by15 smooth-fibre agreements with its generic word: a nonzero difference would have height at least34, contradicting the upper bound32. Exact bounded-degree interpolation verifies the polynomial identities cheaply. For a minimum-norm12 trace, the full pencil moves its intersection with O: with monic degree4 h and c=coeff(M0,t^7), use M=(v*t-u)*M0-v*c*h^2 and divide its cleared chord discriminant by h^6. The resulting branch form has bidegree at most(4,4). Prove D=O+tau-F is primitive nef and that the two explicit Riemann-Roch functions span H0(D). A height12 trace needs23 affine smooth-fibre agreements: height at least50 contradicts the upper bound48. Use the full parity census and translations to prove when the pencil bank exhausts a geometric layer.
lessons.avoid: Fitting exceptional points to choose members, testing only affine parameters, treating zero modular vectors or missing checkpoints as exclusions, reducing rational-function coefficients separately when a joint primitive model exists, or accepting proportional quartics without the rational constant squareclass. Finite trace evaluations require the explicit height bound; polynomial interpolation requires checked degree bounds. Treating the fixed regular norm12 member or M0+lambda*h^2 as its entire genus-one pencil misses the moving finite pole. A smooth normalization need not have a smooth image on the K3. The older rational-V4 deep-trace assertion must be read as a fixed regular-family comparison, not an exhaustive height-ten carrier theorem.
lessons.boundary: All300 pairs of the frozen25 published-R17 pencils are excluded. On direct11952 alternate Q80, all63917 norm8 and49 full moving-contact norm12 pencils have disjoint rational branch images and are individually injective. These63966 pencils exhaust smooth genus-one bisections modulo inherited section translation; all2045792595 pairs are excluded. The replay inherits the certified parent, complete parity census and previous norm8 frames. It does not exclude singular higher-arithmetic-genus images, arbitrary twist ranks, rational normalizations or other parents.
lessons.reopen_when: A singular bisection image with certified genus-one normalization, or another parent or quadratic-cover identity, supplies a new same-cover mechanism. Repeating any smooth genus-one pencil on this alternate-Q80 parent is unnecessary.

lessons.title: Check every stable orthogonal component before using a norm-one obstruction
lessons.when: A K3 rational-marking exclusion is transferred from a split Clifford norm-one modular curve.
lessons.use: Start with the literal lattice and its unique even overlattice to bound the whole projective normalizer. Compute both discriminant signs and every determinant unit in the local GL level, then identify the canonical Q quotient, including the common minus sign from determinant-minus-one orthogonal isometries. For NS0031 this gives Gamma union W_37 Gamma and (X_ns(4) x_X(1) X_0(37))/<w_37 w_ns,4>, genus ten. Reduce Cartan level to obtain a genus-two quotient, certify its differentials and model by a Sturm bound, then determine rational points using full-MW elliptic Chabauty. Pin the elliptic target sign and cusp before applying CM coordinates.
lessons.avoid: Dropping determinant-minus-one isometries, assuming a rational norm-one subgroup is the whole period group, or deducing that a quotient has no rational points because its cover has none. Also avoid replacing a later exact coarse result with an older UNKNOWN catalogue field when rebuilding a queue.
lessons.boundary: The reflection alone refutes the old containment. The completed NS0031 argument separately proves an empty rational noncuspidal non-CM locus; it does not classify rational CM lifts, larger fields, or other lattices. Chabauty at prime5 alone left unresolved cosets; auxiliary primes closed both exact rank-one cases only after full Mordell-Weil groups and their index obligations were proved. Classical Chabauty at rank equal to genus and bounded point searches supply no substitute.
lessons.reopen_when: A different lattice, field or weaker marking changes the arithmetic problem, or a specific defect is found in the full normalizer, canonical descent, quotient identity or exact Chabauty certificate. The original norm-one-containment argument stays invalid.

lessons.title: Reconcile every retained point before preparing another search
lessons.when: A winning chart returns more points than the basis admitted before stopping on its first certified gain.
lessons.use: Retain the entire chart result, replay its exact point maps and test the complete cloud against the terminal subgroup. Certify a reconciled basis before building another landscape. The lower-height cohort added twelve independent directions across five fibres after seven point calls, with zero new point searches during reconciliation; later 07ca9 reconciliation added three more.
lessons.avoid: Treating the first-gain terminal basis as the full known subgroup, dropping unprocessed returned points, or spending another search budget to rediscover them.
lessons.boundary: Cloud reconciliation proves an explicit subgroup lower bound. It does not prove exact rank, saturation, a general yield or point absence. Complete cloud replay needs the saved chart and epoch inputs; an existing PASS label alone is not replay.
lessons.reopen_when: A changed cloud or newly retained witness supplies a candidate outside the certified subgroup; otherwise reuse the reconciled packet.

lessons.title: Prune saved prime blocks before routine subgroup replay
lessons.when: An exact finite-reduction rank packet retains many redundant primes for a fixed point list.
lessons.use: Select rank-increasing prime blocks from the saved binary matrices, then recompute those quotients, exact point identities and the torsion witness. Retain the complete point list and source hashes. For 37 cohort endpoints, 626 of 5,912 saved blocks suffice; all passed in 2.87 seconds with no prime or point search.
lessons.avoid: Recomputing every historical prime, trusting the saved binary matrix as arithmetic proof, silently finding replacement primes, or restarting the search to verify a retained positive result.
lessons.boundary: This greedy selection is sufficient, not minimum cardinality. The replay shares the established finite-group implementation and proves a subgroup lower bound only. Search-selection, map, timing, conductor and full-cloud assertions retain their separate replay inputs and modes. No whole-search speedup is inferred.
lessons.reopen_when: Points, model, native family identity or certificate inputs change, or the selected finite blocks no longer span; a failed witness does not prove dependence.

lessons.title: Construct repeated-root carriers through trace halves and compare complete projective coefficient maps
lessons.when: Seeking two independent gains on one quadratic cover by pairing a singular arithmetic-genus-two carrier with a smooth genus-one pencil.
lessons.use: Derive the tangency quartic and its first jet from a rational half of the generic trace at a smooth fibre. For a complete exclusion, homogenize the two slope parameters to P2 and compare binary sextics against a P1-by-P1 family of a branch quartic times a squared linear factor. Enumerate every projective reduction point and defer a source with a base point. Heights16 and20 provide a conditional rational independence test after a genuine common-cover match.
lessons.avoid: Treating an affine finite-field miss or a singular quartic reduction as a rational exclusion, ignoring infinite parameters, accepting projective proportionality as equality of constant squareclasses, or counting a split inherited carrier as a new direction.
lessons.boundary: All 1,675 pairs of the frozen67 nets and25 pencils are excluded. A retained finite fibre panel gives only a split inherited control; a separate34-probe generic word test also gives no node. These are not an exhaustion of other trace classes, higher-pole carriers, arbitrary twists or rational points on the halving curves.
lessons.reopen_when: A different carrier family, higher-pole chart or arithmetic source gives a new coefficient correspondence, or an explicit two-section twist identity comes with a proved low-genus branch condition. Repeating either closed carrier bank is unnecessary.

lessons.title: Transport a frozen rounded metric across basis changes
lessons.when: A subgroup search policy uses an integer approximation to its numerical height Gram matrix.
lessons.use: Round once for each certified subgroup and retain that decision metric. Under a unimodular basis change U, use the exact congruence U G U^T and transport the subgroup words and cosets. The retained V2 design checks fifteen rebases of seven intermediate subgroups with matching CVP, centre and chart-score data.
lessons.avoid: Recomputing decimal pairings and rounding independently after rebasing; an integer entry can change and alter the policy. Also avoid treating the synthetic three-point wave as a historical simultaneous gain.
lessons.boundary: This is a frozen geometry-only design with zero point searches. The stored rebase checks do not establish a point-search advantage or a rank result. Retrospective nearest-plane diagnostics remain upper bounds in a fixed rounded metric, separate from exact CVP and actual pointed-chart minima.
lessons.reopen_when: The certified subgroup or intended metric changes; freeze a new state before comparing policies. A coordinate change alone should transport the retained state.

lessons.title: Separate seed incidence from repeated and deep acquisition
lessons.when: Choosing parent/fibration populations toward rank32 from retained search history.
lessons.use: Retain complete cohort denominators and frozen features; merge points from the same originating call. Estimate first seed, later acquiring call conditional on exposure, and gain after a prior rank23 subgroup separately. Hold out whole fibrations and check forward cohort transfer before promoting a simple rule. Preserve CPU, elapsed time and censoring scopes. In the new X948 experiment, freeze inequivalent saturated fibrations before evaluating parameters, run a matched baseline, stop first-seed searching at its first gaining cloud, and use address order for separately budgeted amplification.
lessons.avoid: Calling a large first cloud a deep amplification event, calling absent follow-up a stall, learning a parent label under random row splits, conflating X948/X1092 detector differences with causal surface quality, or turning improved seed discrimination into a rank32 tail prediction. Do not remove a blindly selected catalogue rediscovery on the basis of its later novelty comparison.
lessons.boundary: The4482-record census covers33 enumerated retained cohorts, with no claim of distinct curves or complete histories from success-only exports. The broad run has839 seeds,494 later-call amplifiers and five deep amplifiers in2080 rows. Smaller model complexity correlates with deep gains in older R17 cohorts; unchanged forward-cohort models weaken to5/18 versus11/42 and6/18 versus10/42. No tested deep-amplifier rule passes the stated gate. Eight new A1 inputs pass exact admission, but their production advantage remains unestablished. Shared chart/detector effects prevent an intrinsic causal surface inference. The X948 first wave stopped after554 address jobs, before completing Stage1:371 new-fibration seeds and49 baseline seeds, with49 unresolved starting certificates. Its common61-address prefixes show at most1.041 seed/CPU enrichment; amplification did not start. An incomplete first stage cannot support an amplification conclusion.
lessons.reopen_when: A concrete new parent/fibration input or materially different candidate population motivates a separately bounded experiment. Repeated fitting or greater depth on the old stalled27/28 fibres is not the default.

lessons.title: Preserve nonzero conditions when eliminating variables
lessons.when: Constructing a rational or finite-field section chart by dividing equations or eliminating variables.
lessons.use: Record every divisor and elimination coefficient required to be nonzero, and export their small factors separately. The A10 builder retains these in .open.ms instead of multiplying a large polynomial. Reconstruct survivors and test the nonzero conditions, original equations and exact component data before accepting a point.
lessons.avoid: Accepting cleared-numerator solutions after dropping the denominator exclusions, or treating a pole-cancelled section as one with the requested intersection profile. The retained A10 experiments exhibit both failures.
lessons.boundary: These are chart-preservation and filtering lessons from the GF(31)/GF(23 controls. Bounded failure in one chart or prime is not a characteristic-zero obstruction; the finite Hensel lift does not prove a rational point.
lessons.reopen_when: A new chart, elimination or prime changes the denominators or component conditions; preserve the corresponding nonzero-factor export and exact reconstruction checks.

lessons.title: Prove the branch budget before varying a shared-twist auxiliary function
lessons.when: Applying a multi-section quadratic-twist identity to a moving high-rank elliptic parent whose coefficients have large irreducible divisors.
lessons.use: Verify the exact section identities and calculate their heights on the pulled-back surface. Then examine valuations at coefficient divisors before a parameter search. Prove cyclotomic-residue exclusions with irreducible finite reductions and simple local degree-one places; this can force branch points for every rational auxiliary function, including arbitrary zeros and poles. Use the sharp local criterion: an A divisor is removable for some u precisely with i or a primitive cube root in its residue field; a B divisor requires i. Contact orders matter even when the residue is permitted. Impose the remaining global polynomial as a square times one literal squarefree branch polynomial, with infinity and constant squareclasses retained.
lessons.avoid: Transferring a constant-parent twist theorem's independence statement to a moving parent without a height proof, counting a genus-greater-than-one base as an infinite specialization source, or trying a larger auxiliary-function box after an unbounded valuation obstruction.
lessons.boundary: On published R17, alternate Q80 direct11952, Curve302 MW17 and X1092 class1, u=2 gives two independent directions with Gram diag(24,24) on genus21 covers. Every rational auxiliary function in this Mestre identity retains the degree8 A and degree12 B divisors, hence genus at least9. The three additional parent equations have independent portable local and height replays. A separate common-quartic polynomial system would give independent height8 sections with arithmetic-genus5 images if solved; no solution or positive rational base is known on those four MW17 parents.
lessons.reopen_when: A different carrier identity solves a shared-squarefactor equation with branch degree at most4, or an untested parent passes the coefficient-divisor criterion. Repeating the same Mestre auxiliary search on any of the four certified parents cannot meet the base condition. For genus-two nodes, reuse the existing genus-nine halving-locus theorems and preserve their exceptional-chart boundary.

lessons.title: Use finite odd parts to reject high-genus correlated tangent constructions
lessons.when: A universal tangent identity constructs two candidate sections over a quadratic cover from generic inherited sections, but the normalized branch degree is unknown.
lessons.use: Form the shared-ordinate plane cubic, derive its third tangent point symbolically, and clear denominators to a polynomial defining the quadratic squareclass. At an odd integral prime with nonzero reduction, compute the odd-multiplicity part by exact gcds and include infinity. Gauss's lemma proves this reduced branch count is a lower bound in characteristic zero. Require complete input-pair coverage and defer zero reductions.
lessons.avoid: Using the full radical instead of odd multiplicities, ignoring branch at infinity, treating a vanished reduction as a positive candidate or transferring exact reduced genus to an exact characteristic-zero genus.
lessons.boundary: All136 unordered pairs from the published17-section basis, with one tangent each, yield genus at least86. Ordinate signs and pair reversal preserve the branch squareclass. No independence or all-generic-word exclusion follows.
lessons.reopen_when: A different generic pair, an iterated construction or another identity produces a branch divisor within the genus-at-most-one budget; repeating the fixed136 pairs is unnecessary.

lessons.title: Reuse lattice spectra when arithmetic labels change
lessons.when: A rational-marking correction changes the interpretation of a completed geometric census.
lessons.use: Join retained frame spectra to current arithmetic decisions by stable surface IDs. Check identity and original input hashes before reusing the result. For future producers, cache the expensive mathematical kernel by its Gram, algorithm and numeric settings, and attach mutable interpretation separately. Preserve the old execution bundle.
lessons.avoid: Repeating a complete CVP census to refresh32 marking labels, or overwriting the old classifier hash to make a historical certificate look current.
lessons.boundary: The custom-NS producer already joins arithmetic labels after computing the136 spectra, but its checkpoint key includes classifier bytes and successful completion deletes the checkpoint. --check can therefore run all17,825,792 classes. The proposed cache separation is a design lesson, not an implemented replay shortcut or a proof of arithmetic admission.
lessons.reopen_when: A Gram, mathematical domain or enumeration algorithm changes, or an explicitly scoped independent arithmetic replay is needed.

lessons.title: Search each shared cover once, then intersect certified parameter sets
lessons.when: Many simultaneous-square pair covers reuse the same individual polynomial covers and projective height box.
lessons.use: Search the80 Fermigier covers once, retaining exact parameter/root pairs and projective residue filters. Intersect those parameter sets for all3160 unordered pairs, then verify each square identity separately. Reuse the completed height200000 output before considering further enumeration.
lessons.avoid: Repeating the individual point search for every pair, or accepting a square product when neither factor is separately square.
lessons.boundary: The negative result covers reduced T=a/b with b>0 and max(|a|,b)<=200000 only. Both prescribed anchors survive; it is not a global rational-point theorem. Exact frozen-manifest replay also needs the historical inputs; the current producer scans a mutable prior-parameter inventory.
lessons.reopen_when: A mathematically motivated new domain or cover family is explicitly in scope; preserve exact model, coordinate and height-box identities before reusing parameter sets.

lessons.title: Prove minimality on the invariant gcd before factoring the discriminant
lessons.when: An integral endpoint needs a minimal-model certificate but full discriminant factorization is costly.
lessons.use: Restrict possible nonminimal primes to gcd(c4,c6). At each, first test the necessary valuations4,6,12 of c4,c6,Delta; only surviving primes need the scaled-invariant integral-model test. For the full11952 rank27 model, gcd75 leaves only3 and5 and both fail the valuations. Exact coordinate transport keeps the point-independence proof separate.
lessons.avoid: Making complete discriminant factorization or a conductor calculation a prerequisite for this minimality or rank-lower-bound proof.
lessons.boundary: The standalone fast path requires integral coefficients, nonzero evaluated invariants and invariant gcd at most10^8; outside its gate it fails closed. The201-model audit uses local checks at2,3 and gcd primes. Minimality does not certify conductor, saturation or an exact rank.
lessons.reopen_when: A different model fails the fast gate or passes the necessary valuation test; use the retained scaled-invariant or local-minimality checks before requesting full factorization.

lessons.title: Keep fixed inventory snapshots separate from the current census
lessons.when: Routing a conductor, curve-count or display question that cites a dated inventory refresh.
lessons.use: Use the generated current inventory and database for present selection. Use each dated snapshot only for its named roster, cutoff and certificate claims; preserve it when later certified additions change the count.
lessons.avoid: Treating a 291-, 321- or 445-curve snapshot as the current census, or restarting its historical conductor campaign during routine cleanup.
lessons.boundary: The snapshot certificates establish their stated bounded conductor facts. They do not silently include later foundry results, and a current inventory count does not strengthen any snapshot theorem.
lessons.reopen_when: A new immutable snapshot has been independently checked, added to the authority ledger and selected by the current manifest.

lessons.title: Treat a split bisection as a candidate until exact admission closes it
lessons.when: Specializing a rational conic or bisection whose branch value is a nonzero rational square.
lessons.use: Verify the generic trace and factor-free map identities, classify incidence with an exact numerator/denominator square receipt, and retain one nonramified branch. Supply the sealed full finite-reduction footprint to an independent admission check. A candidate becomes a seed only with an explicit increased-rank certificate. For an in-span column, use bounded halving/cycle classification; only its resulting exact integer relation proves inheritance. Preserve a step-cap or deficient footprint as UNKNOWN.
lessons.avoid: Calling a nonzero split a new Mordell--Weil direction, counting its trace companion as another seed, treating ramification as an extra point, or declaring a finite-column miss to be dependence.
lessons.boundary: The Euclidean formula and four replayed inherited relations cover their stated generic trace charts, sealed fibres and finite footprints. They do not classify every split in the atlas, prove an upper rank bound, or establish that a different fibre has no new direction.
lessons.reopen_when: A newly sealed fibre supplies an explicit injective finite footprint and branch point, or a different generic chart changes the map and incidence hypotheses.

lessons.title: Separate a stopped controller's replay interface from the current programme
lessons.when: Reading a retained foundry or pilot note during cleanup, candidate selection, or incident recovery.
lessons.use: Read MATH_STATUS.json and the elliptic-curve programme map before acting. Treat a terminal report, frozen manifest, controller state and command block as evidence for the recorded run; preserve them for certificate audit, then follow the separately selected current route.
lessons.avoid: Invoking launch, resume or allocation commands from a stopped protocol, treating a report named live or a READY row as a live process, or extending a finite panel merely because its source still contains an operational policy.
lessons.boundary: A stopped receipt preserves completed lower-bound certificates, inputs and bounded exposures. It does not make their policy current, establish an upper bound, or invalidate a separately authorized successor campaign.
lessons.reopen_when: A new controller has an explicit mathematical gate, frozen input and budget, a declared relation to prior receipts, and authorization through the current programme rather than through an old command block.

lessons.title: Deduplicate cumulative transcripts before exact point recognition
lessons.when: Reconstructing a historical chart or checkpoint record that stores cumulative snapshots and repeated rational-point evidence.
lessons.use: Bind records by their complete seed and epoch path, retain only the maximal cumulative snapshot for each stage, and deduplicate point evidence before arithmetic recognition. Use high-precision height coordinates only to propose a lattice word; verify every promoted word by exact elliptic-curve group equality. Keep unbound point evidence as UNKNOWN.
lessons.avoid: Counting cumulative snapshots as fresh exposure, accepting numerical coordinates as a point identity, treating unbound evidence as zero exposure, or continuing a historical replay into downstream experiments by default.
lessons.boundary: The Curve302 adapter reduces a fixed historical transcript with about 1.27 million cumulative chart records to a normalized ledger. Its recognition and exposure results apply only to its bound raw paths and schema; they are not prospective selection evidence or a portable arithmetic certificate.
lessons.reopen_when: A new transcript has a different schema, path identity, basis, or point-evidence join and is supplied with immutable inputs and an independently stated replay purpose.

lessons.title: Construct a complete quotient in its certifying basis
lessons.when: A filtered orbit or survivor export is used to define a complete mod-2 or lattice-quotient search universe.
lessons.use: State the exported subset and its coordinate basis explicitly. Generate the full quotient directly in the certified parent basis, transport masks by the exact basis map, then use the filtered export only as an independent subset/count check. Freeze the resulting universe before score or point-search outcomes enter selection.
lessons.avoid: Treating a rational-survivor TSV as every quotient class, mixing its reduced masks with parent-basis words, or treating a preflight/schema failure as arithmetic search evidence.
lessons.boundary: The V4 determinant-1092 panel builds all 2^17 parent-basis masks and checks the 104,978 exported norm-8/10/12 survivors as a subset. Its 4,096 finite no-gain charts do not establish complete pointed-chart coverage, exact rank, or absence of a jump.
lessons.reopen_when: The quotient, basis transport, equivalence relation, survivor predicate, or certified subgroup changes.

lessons.title: Close a matched frame panel with its terminal receipt before changing frames
lessons.when: Comparing prospective fibration or parent frames under a frozen score, controls, and point-search policy.
lessons.use: Bind the full score order, matched control prefix, model transform, per-endpoint limits, and both search and replay receipts. If a representation correction is necessary, certify the exact coordinate and section transforms while preserving the score and selection rule. Charge failed preparation separately. Release a successor frame only after every endpoint has a terminal classification and the frozen panel receipt records its complete exposure.
lessons.avoid: Treating a stale controller PID or STARTED label as a live process; retuning scores after a coordinate correction; calling a finite no-gain panel a rank bound or a frame exclusion; or charging only successful point-search time when comparing frame cost.
lessons.boundary: The class1 64-plus-16 and class3 32-plus-8 X1092 panels each completed at their stated lower bound17 and received NO_EVIDENCE_CURRENT_SEARCH_PRODUCTIVE. They establish only those matched exposures. They do not compare all frames, prove a rank upper bound for any fibre, or show that a corrected representation cannot be productive under a different protocol.
lessons.reopen_when: A distinct frame or protocol has a new mathematical gate, frozen score/control relationship, exact model transport, declared budget, and authorization through the current programme.

lessons.title: Take residual localized 2-torsion before quotienting known Kummer classes
lessons.when: Using a cubic field class group and bad-prime localization as a prospective feature for a known Mordell--Weil subgroup.
lessons.use: Form the full localized finite group A_S = Cl(K)/<S>, extract its actual order-two subgroup A_S[2] from Smith data, then quotient by the localized known Kummer-class image. Transport the completed-square root through the certified field isomorphism and require unconditional field and BNF certificates. Keep a timeout or failed backend as a null feature and leave the blinded point-search ledger sealed.
lessons.avoid: Replacing A_S[2]/<c_S(G_i)> by Cl(K)/(2Cl(K)+<S,c(G_i)>), assuming A[2] and A/2A have the same embedded subgroup, or unsealing a detector from a GRH-only or partial BNF result.
lessons.boundary: The Z/4, Z/8, and localized Z/8/<2> fixtures establish the quotient distinction and the Phase-0 cohort fixes a rank-blind population. No Phase-1 row has a certified quotient value, so this does not produce a Selmer dimension, a rank conclusion, or a predictor result.
lessons.reopen_when: A separately scoped experiment has complete unconditional BNF records for its whole frozen cohort and a detector protocol bound to the resulting feature-file hash.

lessons.title: Quotient the complete known Kummer subgroup before local Selmer cuts
lessons.when: A record fibre has a certified global squareclass upper envelope, known rational points and only a partial set of local conditions.
lessons.use: Embed and certify every known Kummer row in the global envelope before forming local equations, then work in the explicit quotient coordinates. Add certified local rows monotonically. A zero quotient kernel proves closure for the supplied global envelope; use a parity refinement only after its total-Selmer parity hypothesis is certified.
lessons.avoid: Subtracting displayed Mordell--Weil ranks without exact Kummer independence, treating a BNF timeout or relation plateau as a global envelope, or calling a nonzero partial kernel an exact residual Selmer quotient.
lessons.boundary: The current R17 record-fibre interfaces preserve 29 Kummer rows and exact local-matrix machinery, but no certified BNF or equivalent global envelope. Their residual groups remain UNKNOWN; the retained timeouts are neither upper bounds nor candidate exclusions.
lessons.reopen_when: A certified BNF, ray-class calculation, or other complete global squareclass provider supplies the required envelope and local maps.

lessons.title: Retain unfactored relation tails as exact ideal-graph vertices
lessons.when: Collecting principal-ideal relations for a relative class or Selmer quotient when full cofactor factorization is too expensive.
lessons.use: Keep the original ideal HNF, reduction multipliers, exact principal generator, proved factor-base valuations, and the reduced unfactored residual ideal. Add an edge only after the complete principal identity and every recorded prime-ideal valuation verify. Generate projectively distinct short elements inside a residual ideal, and monitor graph dependencies against new outside-prime vertices before spending another tranche.
lessons.avoid: Treating a reduced-ideal collision without its multipliers as a principal relation; discarding an unfactored tail as zero evidence; inserting a guessed prime factor; counting rational multiples as fresh rows; or promoting an underdense finite graph to a class-group or Selmer bound.
lessons.boundary: On the retained MW29-relative 356/385 tranches, exact residual-tail and outside-prime relations still had zero quotient-rank gain and no graph dependencies. The raw ledgers are local-only, so this records a relation-construction and stopping rule, not a portable class-group computation, upper bound, or proof that another construction cannot work.
lessons.reopen_when: A certified global F2 quotient generator or upper bound, a complete ray-class provider, or an independently justified relation family supplies a different graph-growth mechanism.

lessons.title: Run higher Selmer descent only on the residual complement
lessons.when: A complete 2-Selmer computation contains a certified rational Kummer block and higher 4- or 8-Selmer images are needed for a rank bound.
lessons.use: Define higher stages as their images in the complete 2-Selmer group, quotient by the known rational block, and freeze the complete all-place matrix before labels are opened. Pair and construct covers only on a basis of that complement while retaining the entire linear kernel. The first Cassels--Tate drop has even codimension. Stop as soon as a certified image equals the known rational block: later descent cannot improve the rank bound.
lessons.avoid: Treating 2-, 4-, and 8-Selmer groups as literal nested objects without their image maps; re-running higher descent on known rational classes; enumerating every nonzero residual class; inferring the image dimension from individual basis-cover outcomes; or calling an incomplete descent, BNF timeout, or point-search miss an upper bound.
lessons.boundary: For the R17 record pair, the complete 2-Selmer group and all higher-image dimensions remain UNKNOWN. The known 12-dimensional residual rational block is only a lower floor; this protocol neither supplies its missing global envelope nor explains the rank jump.
lessons.reopen_when: A certified complete global 2-Selmer envelope, all-place local matrices, immutable cover inputs, and a separately scoped descent certificate are available.

lessons.title: Peel only isolated norm obstructions before class construction
lessons.when: A finite dictionary of cubic-field elements is proposed for an unramified Kummer or class-construction word.
lessons.use: Recompute every norm exactly. Exclude the declared bad support, remove only generators with an isolated nonsquare norm remainder, and repeat until stable. Retain shared-support generators because products can cancel. For an elliptic interpretation, first prove that every bad elliptic place is in the excluded support.
lessons.avoid: Eliminating every individually ramified generator, treating a residual dictionary as unramified, or promoting zero retained dictionary capacity to a curve, Selmer, or rank exclusion.
lessons.boundary: The frozen 428-generator retrospective panel peels every coefficient in one round and has zero retained capacity. It rejects only those constructed dictionaries; a known-soluble reference still has genuine additional directions.
lessons.reopen_when: The cubic, forbidden support or dictionary changes; added generators can introduce cancellations and invalidate a prior forced-zero conclusion.

lessons.title: Freeze intake selection before a bounded seed-to-V3 funnel
lessons.when: Reducing a large family of parameterized elliptic curves to a small number of point-search seeds.
lessons.use: Fix the primitive address domain, deduplication relation, feature definitions, quotas, ties and control allocation before the intake. Preserve every draw, rejection, selected input and replay digest. Certify the inherited subgroup and the first independent point exactly before handing an M18 packet to V3.
lessons.avoid: Refilling a quota after point outcomes, using a known later point in selection, promoting a local score or split cover to an independent point, or treating a bounded miss as an exclusion of the fibre or family.
lessons.boundary: The determinant1092 funnel replayed a ten-million-address intake and a separate conic-splitting follow-up. It produced three M18 fibres and one rank-at-least-21 specialization, but proves neither a score-prediction theorem nor a rank upper bound for the remaining population.
lessons.reopen_when: A new population, selector or point-search budget is mathematically justified, versioned, independently replayable and explicitly in scope.

lessons.title: Balance structural address features before dispatch
lessons.when: Building a score-versus-control comparison from a deterministic rational-address enumerator.
lessons.use: Freeze a score-independent, hash-based control allocator and audit it before point work against sign, height, prefix, and every other feature induced by the address encoding. Preserve the full selection and counts. If the audit fails, stop dispatch, retain the aborted cohort, and use a disjoint corrected window.
lessons.avoid: Calling a deterministic stride an unbiased control merely because it does not read the score; combining a confounded pilot with a corrected cohort; or promoting a bounded no-gain endpoint to evidence that the score has no value.
lessons.boundary: The class1 v1 rule selected indices congruent to 7 modulo 8, but odd addresses encode negative rationals. The audit stopped v1 after one control call. V2 used a disjoint 65,536-address window with 8,192 hash-selected controls (4,153 positive and 4,039 negative), then completed 1,920 calls with no gain beyond rank 17. This establishes the control-integrity correction, not score efficacy or a rank bound.
lessons.reopen_when: The address enumerator, control allocator, feature set, outcome definition, or exposure budget changes.

lessons.title: Score retrospective next moves with complete denominator accounting
lessons.when: Testing a proposed next-direction score against a sealed sequence of acquisitions on a known curve.
lessons.use: Freeze each candidate vocabulary independently of the acquired target and rank candidates only from the current prefix. Report vocabulary coverage separately; include absent targets in the event denominator and loss; exclude the admitted quotient span; use worst-rank tie handling; and aggregate by run when runs share a curve, metric, or point vocabulary. Compare to a fixed nonadaptive baseline rather than to a correlation built from the same metric.
lessons.avoid: Inserting a held-out target into its own vocabulary, deleting out-of-vocabulary events, treating tied final-stage candidates as unique top-one hits, calling 180 acquisitions independent trials, or promoting a same-metric correlation to a prospective predictor.
lessons.boundary: On the retained Curve302 trajectories, neither tested adaptive score beat static quotient norm in its bounded literal-vector vocabulary. Coverage was 49/180 and 70/180, so this rejects only those retrospective score/vocabulary pairs. The full input and output bundle is not shipped with this checkout, and no prospective predictor, propagation theorem, or rank bound follows.
lessons.reopen_when: A new prospective protocol freezes an outcome-independent candidate universe, a target-aligned endpoint, a complete immutable input bundle, tie rules, and a separately justified control population.

lessons.title: Bind pointed-search continuations to maps, finite state, and archived observations
lessons.when: Replacing a point-search backend or continuing a fixed roster of pointed-quartic charts from a certified Mordell--Weil subgroup.
lessons.use: Freeze the exact chart maps, reduced model, ordered roster, executable identity, limits, raw result fields, and an explicit infinity check before comparing backends. Replay maps, square hits, returned points, and finite independence without rediscovering them. Preload a declared prime bank once for a fixed basis, and rotate the entire prior observation state into an immutable archive before producing the next live state. Require every continuation to bind its parent-state key and each map index exactly once.
lessons.avoid: Comparing affine square sets while ignoring infinity, roster order, return codes, or duplicate records; treating a timeout as coverage of an unrecorded denominator prefix; mixing PARI output with a GMP transcript; dropping prior observations during state rotation; or presenting a point-cloud replay as exact rank or saturation.
lessons.boundary: On the retained rank-26 and rank-22 controls, map and state replays validate the completed fixed 301-box PARI rosters and their lower-bound clouds. The measured prime-preload improvement and backend timings apply to the declared controls only; finite no-gain boxes and complete clouds remain lower-bound evidence, not a speed theorem or rank upper bound.
